q: Who in a small company should sign off the carbon figures before they go to a buyer or bank?
title: Who signs off company carbon figures
short: A director or owner, after someone other than the preparer has checked them. Carbon figures now go into loan files, buyer contracts and CBAM declarations, so treat them like financial numbers: one person prepares, another reviews, and a named director approves the final version and the date it was sent.

ol: Preparer: plant or accounts staff who enter the data.
Reviewer: someone else checks totals against invoices.
Approver: a director signs off and records the date.

p: A wrong figure sent to a lender or EU importer is hard to withdraw. A sign-off trail shows the figure was checked and who to ask about it.
Which figure went to whom, on what date, and on what basis. Buyers often ask months later.

senseible: Senseible keeps every figure linked to its source invoice or bill with a fingerprint, so a verifier can trace a total back to the documents it came from.
